title: act-mcp tool contract: arguments and structured results of the four tools (MCP 2026-07-28)
description: Machine-readable half of docs/adr/0001-tool-contract.md and docs/tool-contract.md. Each tool has two entries under $defs: '<tool>_args' (the tools/call params.arguments object) and '<tool>_result' (the JSON object the server puts in result.structuredContent). 'tool_error' is the shape of structuredContent on an isError:true tool result. This root schema validates nothing by itself: scripts/validate_tool_contract.py selects one $defs entry as the schema root and copies $defs along so the internal '#/$defs/...' refs keep resolving. The prose contract is the ADR; ADR, docs/tool-contract.md, the fixture set and this file are held in lockstep by that script.
x-nullability: A value is either present with its correct type or the key is absent. JSON null is never valid anywhere in this contract; unknown is expressed by omission (same policy as ADR-0002 section 2.1). Every object here is additionalProperties:false.

x-run-status.note: The five terminal names are the SAME vocabulary as .evidence run_status in schema/evidence.schema.json and schema/run-meta.schema.json. 'succeeded' is not a status value anywhere in this project.

invalid_arguments.meaning: A required argument is missing, an argument has the wrong JSON type, or a value violates its length bound or pattern. detail.errors lists every offending instance path, so the caller self-corrects in one round trip.

unknown_argument.meaning: An argument the tool does not define was supplied (including a caller-supplied run_id: run ids are server-generated only). Detail names each unexpected key and the accepted set.

workspace_not_found.meaning: The workspace directory (server CWD, or --workspace) does not exist, is not a directory, or is not readable.

not_a_git_repository.meaning: The workspace is not inside a git work tree, so a commit cannot be resolved or checked out inside it. git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed.

workflows_dir_missing.meaning: <workspace>/.github/workflows is absent, is not a directory, or contains no *.yml / *.yaml file. This is the gate that says 'this directory is not a GitHub Actions repository'.

act_missing.meaning: The act binary was not found on PATH, is not executable, or is older than the minimum supported version. Cached probe (30s), so retrying after installing act succeeds.
act_missing.detail: {probed: [string], reason: not_found | not_executable | too_old, found_version?: string, minimum_version?: string}

docker_unreachable.meaning: No container runtime answered (docker info, or the configured --container-daemon-socket, failed or timed out). Cached probe (30s).

workflow_not_found.meaning: No file under .github/workflows matches the requested workflow, or it matched only a workflow name: key that resolves to a file that does not exist. Detail lists the valid options so the caller self-corrects in one round trip.

ambiguous_workflow.meaning: More than one file matches the requested workflow name (for example bench.yml and bench.yaml, or two files declaring the same name: key). The caller must disambiguate by passing the file name.

task_not_found.meaning: The resolved workflow declares no job with that id (the value that act -j <job> would receive). Detail lists the job ids in that file.

commit_unknown.meaning: The commit does not resolve in the workspace repository (git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit} failed). act-mcp never fetches: a commit the local clone does not have is a caller error, not a network task.

commit_ambiguous.meaning: An abbreviated commit matches more than one object. Supply a longer prefix (40 hex is never ambiguous).

isolation_failed.meaning: ADR-0003 could not produce a working tree for the requested commit: the running policy refuses a commit other than HEAD (head-only mode), or the temporary worktree could not be created or removed. The run was not started.
isolation_failed.detail: {mode: head_only | worktree, requested: string, head: string, reason: string}

workspace_busy.meaning: Another act run holds the workspace single-flight lock (ADR-0003 / ADR-0004). There is no queue: the call fails immediately and detail names the run in flight so the caller can poll it or cancel it.

too_many_runs.meaning: The server-wide concurrent-act-run cap (--max-concurrent-runs, default 2) is reached across all workspaces.

idempotency_conflict.meaning: The supplied idempotency_key is already remembered for a DIFFERENT (workflow, task, category, commit) tuple. The server will not silently start a second run under a key that already means something else.
idempotency_conflict.detail: {idempotency_key: string, run_id: run_id, previous: object, requested: object}

run_not_found.meaning: No run with that run_id is known to this server process. Run state is in memory (ADR-0004); after a restart or retention eviction the durable trace is .evidence/runs/<run_id>/, which is not polled by run_status.

internal_error.meaning: The server failed in a way it did not predict, before any run was created. No run exists and nothing was written.

act_spawn_failed.meaning: act could not be started (fork/exec failure, bad working directory, argument building blew up). Terminal run status 'error'; the run exists and its (empty) log is on disk.

act_crashed.meaning: act died by signal, or was reaped without an exit status, for a reason that is not a timeout and not a cancel. Terminal run status 'error'.

runner_internal_error.meaning: The supervisor failed mid-run after act was started (state machine inconsistency, worktree vanished, log pipe died). Terminal run status 'error'; whatever evidence already landed stays published.

evidence_write_failed.meaning: act finished but the evidence the run existed to produce could not be written (EACCES, ENOSPC, read-only evidence root). The run is failed on purpose: a silent success with no file is the worst outcome. meta.json may be absent for these runs.

evidence_path_exists.meaning: The evidence file this run was about to publish already exists (ADR-0002 section 6.2). That means a run_id collision, which is a bug worth surfacing rather than merging into someone else's file. Terminal run status 'error'.

evidence_path_escape.meaning: A path derived from caller-controlled or payload-controlled input resolved outside the evidence root, or through a symlink (ADR-0002 section 6.3). The write was refused; terminal run status 'error'.

run_id.description: Server-generated run identity; shape pinned by ADR-0002 section 1.2 so ls order is chronological. Never supplied by a caller.

timestamp.description: UTC instant, always Z (never +00:00), fractional seconds optional; writers canonicalise to millisecond precision. Same rule as ADR-0002 section 2.2.

relpath.description: Workspace-relative (or evidence-root-relative) path, forward slashes, no leading /, no . or .. segment, no absolute host path anywhere in a tool result.

workflow_name.description: Workflow identity as a caller types it: basename without extension (coverage), basename with .yml/.yaml, or the workspace-relative path .github/workflows/<file>. Case sensitive. Two consecutive dots are forbidden anywhere, so no '..' traversal segment is expressible; a leading '/' or '-' is not matchable. ADR-0001 section 2.2.

task_id.description: Job id declared in the resolved workflow file; exactly what act -j receives (ADR-0001 section 2.3). Same dot rule as workflow_name: '..' is not expressible.

category.description: OPEN vocabulary, deliberately not a closed enum: benchmark and coverage are the two known values in v1, any other shape-legal value runs the job and produces no evidence. ADR-0001 section 2.4 states the reason.

commit_input.description: Commit as a caller types it: 7 to 40 hex digits, either case, normalized to lowercase before resolution. No whitespace, no .., no ~, no leading - (ADR-0001 section 2.5).

commit_full.description: Resolved commit: full lowercase 40-hex SHA. Every result field named commit uses this, never the caller's abbreviation.

warning_code.description: OPEN vocabulary of machine-readable caveats. Same vocabulary as meta.json warnings[] in ADR-0002 section 5.1, plus the tool-level members listed in docs/tool-contract.md. Adding a member is additive; an unknown code is never fatal.

error_code.description: CLOSED set of machine-readable tool error codes. Every member is documented in docs/adr/0001-tool-contract.md section 5.3 and docs/tool-contract.md; x-error-codes in this file carries isError / retryable / owning tools per member. A client that receives a code it does not know MUST treat the call as a failed tool call (never as success) and MUST NOT retry blindly.

error.description: The typed error payload. Present in structuredContent of every isError:true tool result (as the whole object), and as the 'error' member of a run result whose terminal status is 'error'.

message.description: One human-readable sentence, no trailing newline, secret values already redacted. Never a stack trace, never a host absolute path.

retryable.description: Whether calling again unchanged could possibly succeed, taken from the table in ADR-0001 section 5.3. Callers MUST NOT retry a retryable:true error in a tight loop.

detail.description: Per-code machine-readable context; shape documented per code in x-error-codes. Keys listed there are always present for that code, extra keys are allowed. Must not exceed 4096 bytes when compactly serialized; lists are truncated rather than truncated mid-element.

tool_error.description: The whole structuredContent object of an isError:true result: exactly one error member and nothing else.

secret_map.description: Secret passthrough. Values never appear in argv, in any file under .evidence, in log_tail, or in a tool result; the runner redacts them at the source (mact-f1w.8 / .13).

input_map.description: workflow_dispatch-style inputs, passed as act --input key=value in sorted key order so argv is stable and golden-testable.

log_tail_bytes.description: How much log tail to return. The server truncates to a UTF-8 boundary at the last complete line that fits.

log_tail.description: Last lines of act's rendered log, redacted, workspace and evidence absolute paths replaced by <WORKSPACE> and <EVIDENCE>. Length is capped in BYTES by log_tail_bytes; maxLength here is the maximum allowed request (65536).

status.description: Run state. pending/running are non-terminal and reachable only through run_status or a wait:false call; the other five are terminal and are the SAME names as .evidence run_status (ADR-0002).

phase.description: Coarse progress inside the supervisor (ADR-0004 owns transitions). Advisory: a client may display it, nothing may branch on it. Unknown values are ignored.

run_view.description: The canonical view of one run, returned by run_status(run_id) and, with the extra member 'deduplicated', by run_workflow. Fields the caller asked for by name in the ticket are all here: run_id, status, workflow_file, job (named 'task'), commit, started_at, duration_ms, evidence_files, evidence_record_count, log_tail, error.

terminal.description: Redundant with status by design: a client polling run_status should not need a status table to decide whether to poll again.

workflow.description: Resolved workflow identity: file basename without .yml/.yaml. Never a path, never re-derived from logs. Same value as the evidence envelope's workflow field.

duration_ms.description: Wall duration in ms: total run duration once terminal, elapsed-so-far while pending/running. Omitted only when the clock is not known (act never started).

exit_code.description: act's wait(2) code. Absent when act produced no exit status (signalled, spawn failure) and always absent for pending/running.

evidence_files.description: The JSONL evidence files this run published, relative to the evidence root (ADR-0002 section 1.1). Empty array means the run produced none, which is legitimate for an unknown category and for a run that died before extraction. meta.json and act.jsonl are NOT listed here: they are audit paths, not the contract.

evidence_record_count.description: Total records across evidence_files. Zero is meaningful (ran, found nothing); it is not an error.

run_summary.description: Compact entry for the run_status listing (no run_id given). Deliberately small: the listing is a recovery aid after a lost run_id, not a log viewer.

run_workflow_args.description: tools/call params.arguments for run_workflow. All four identity fields are required; nothing else may be supplied except the listed optionals.

wait.description: true (default): block until the run reaches a terminal state or timeout_secs expires, whichever comes first. false: return as soon as the run is registered, status running. A run outlives the request either way.

timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock budget for the act run and therefore for the blocking wait: at expiry the act process group is killed as a group and the run ends 'timed_out'. Defaults are per category and owned by ADR-0004 (v1: coverage 900, benchmark 1800, anything else 1800).

idempotency_key.description: Optional caller-side dedup token. A repeat call with the same key and the same (workflow, task, category, commit) returns the remembered run instead of starting a second one; same key with a different tuple is idempotency_conflict. Remembered in memory only, for as long as run state is retained (ADR-0004).

run_workflow_result.description: structuredContent of a successful (isError:false) run_workflow call: run_view plus 'deduplicated'. Spelled out field-for-field instead of by $ref so a generated Rust struct and this file can be diffed mechanically; scripts/validate_tool_contract.py asserts the field set equals run_view's plus 'deduplicated'.

deduplicated.description: True when this result is a remembered run found through idempotency_key rather than a run started by this call.

list_tasks_args.description: tools/call params.arguments for list_tasks. No argument may name a path: the tool only ever reads the server's own workspace (mact-f1w.13).

include_steps.description: Also return each job's step summary (name, uses). Off by default: a big workflow's step list is the bulk of the payload.

list_tasks_result.description: structuredContent for list_tasks. A workflow file that fails to parse is reported with an error member; it never fails the call.

display.description: The workflow's name: key if it declares one; absent otherwise.

parse_error.description: Why this one file could not be read. Its own code namespace, deliberately separate from the tool-level error codes: a broken workflow file is data reported inside a successful call, never a failed call (one bad file must not break discovery).

uses_composite.description: True when the job or one of its steps references a remote or local reusable workflow/action (act needs network or a checkout to resolve it).

category_hint.description: ADVISORY best-effort guess so a caller can pick a benchmark or coverage job without guessing: benchmark | coverage | other. Never authoritative: the caller still passes category explicitly.

run_status_args.description: tools/call params.arguments for run_status. With run_id: that run. Without it: the bounded recent/active listing.

limit.description: Listing mode only: how many runs to return, newest first.

run_status_result.description: structuredContent for run_status. Exactly one of run / runs is present, and the server does not validate that for you beyond the schemas: run iff run_id was supplied.

active_count.description: Runs currently non-terminal in this server process, whether or not they are in the returned page.

truncated.description: True when older finished runs were dropped from the page (retention window from ADR-0004).

cancel_run_result.description: structuredContent for cancel_run. Cancelling a terminal run is NOT an error: cancel is idempotent and reports what was already true.

already_terminal.description: True when the run was already terminal before this call; cancel_requested_at is then absent and status is the old terminal status, not cancelled.

kill.description: How the act process group was taken down (ADR-0004 owns the mechanics). Absent for a queued run that never started a process and for an already_terminal run.
